agent_answer.notes: The corpus contains 20 synthetic papers (S001-S020), each comparing a retrieval-augmented condition against a non-retrieval baseline (and sometimes a fine-tuning condition) on a factual-accuracy metric (fraction/proportion of factually correct answers) or a hallucination metric (share of answers containing at least one unsupported statement). Each paper's abstract states its conclusion on whether retrieval augmentation improves factual accuracy. Tally: 12 papers report a clear improvement (higher accuracy and/or fewer hallucinations), 4 report no measurable change, and 4 report a decrease in accuracy / increase in hallucination. Because the corpus is mixed, the overall answer to 'Does RAG improve the factual accuracy of LLM-generated answers?' is: it depends on the setting — RAG improves accuracy in the majority (12/20) of papers, has no effect in 4, and harms accuracy in 4. Supporting per-paper numbers were recorded as claims (e.g., S002 baseline 0.505 vs RAG 0.571; S003 783/1000 vs 77.4%; S009 53.8% vs 0.465).
